chapter: Lucky Millinder and Duke Ellington's band, 1948-52
title: Tricky Sam Nanton's plunger chair
summary: Tricky Sam urged Jackson to take his chair; Jackson thought he never could but learned Tricky's solos from records.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Growl, plunger and derby: the trumpet mute tradition

blocks.x: And that's when I first got a chance to work with Sandy, and, really, you know what Sandy -- Tricky used to tell me all the time, you know, -- Tricky had a real high voice -- he said, 'Gee whiz, when are you going to give me a break? When are you going to sit in my chair, man? You
sit over there in Tizol's chair all the time." I told him, I said, "It'll never happen. I'll never try to play -- I'll never be able to grab that plunger. No, no." And where did I wind up?
-- the only one that ever really replaced him.
Yeah. Well, I tried, you know, because I had all the records, you see. It wasn't that hard because I heard every note he played. I knew all his solos, in fact.
